rationale: Compound: ⲣⲙ̄- ('man of') + ⲁⲛ- (genitive linker) + ⲧⲡⲉ ('above, heaven') = 'man of the height, heaven-man.' Used here for the Five Sons of First Man as 'the five heaven-men.' Distinct from ⲡⲣⲙⲛⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ 'Man of Light.'

Standard Coptic ⲁϣⲉ 'hang, suspend.' Recurs through this kephalaion as the cosmogonic verb for setting the Zones in their cosmic positions. Lycopolitan inflected forms: ⲁϩⲉⲓϣⲉ (3sg.m. perfect), ⲁϩⲉϣⲧ (qualitative or perfect with object suffix?), ⲁϣⲉ (infinitive). The cosmic 'hanging' of zone-within-zone is the core image of K.37.
Lyc reflex of ϩⲓϩⲟⲩⲛ 'on the inside, within.' Spatial preposition expressing nested containment — central to the chapter's image of Zones-within-Zones.

Abstract: ⲙⲛⲧ- + ϫⲁϫⲉ ('enemy') = 'state-of-being-enemy, enmity.' Capitalized here as a cosmic principle = the personified hostile dark powers bound within the cosmic Zones. Standard Coptic, but warrants explicit listing for Manichaean cosmological register.

proposed_english: the Ancient One / the Old Man
rationale: Already in glossary as 'the Ancient One' for cosmic-archonic register. In the anthropological context of K.38, the same term denotes the Manichaean 'Old Man' (palaios anthrōpos) — the fleshly dark self whom the Light-Mind binds within the body. Worth annotating that the cosmic Ancient One and the inner Old Man are correspondentially identified: the same hostile principle operates at cosmic and microcosmic registers.

Hapax in this corpus; lexeme of uncertain root. Context requires a noun for the variability the disciple observes in the saint, contrasting with the Mind of Light's intrinsic immutability. Possibly Lyc form of ⲡⲱϣⲥ 'splitting, division' or ⲃⲗ̄ⲥ̄ 'weakness/decay.' Flag for parallels.

Verb of uncertain root used here of the Mind of Light entering the 'smallness' of the body. Context demands a verb of narrowing/confinement. May be related to a Coptic root for tightness or to a verb of dwelling-in-narrow-place.
Lycopolitan compound place-noun: ⲡⲥⲁ-ⲛ-ϩⲟⲩⲛ 'the inside-side.' Used here for nested zones: 'a Zone of the inside of another Zone.' Spatial-architectural cosmological term.
